title: Malignant Ovarian Germ Cell Tumors: Dysgerminoma & Yolk Sac
subject: ss-gynaecological-oncology
refs: DeVita, Hellman, and Rosenberg's Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology 11e Ch 85
NCCN Clinical Practice Guidelines in Oncology: Ovarian Cancer (2024)

steps.say: Malignant germ cell neoplasms occur predominantly in adolescent and young adult females. Dysgerminoma represents the most prevalent histological variant, identical morphologically to testicular seminoma.
steps.tx: **Dysgerminoma** is the **most common MOGCT** (malignant ovarian germ cell tumor), accounting for **30-40%** (**30** to **40** percent) of cases with **median age 15-20** (**15** to **20** years). It uniquely exhibits **bilateral involvement 10-15%** (**10** to **15** percent) at initial diagnosis, whereas other malignant germ cell variants are almost universally unilateral.

steps.say: Serum tumor biomarkers play an indispensable role in distinguishing distinct histological variants. Dysgerminoma secretes lactate dehydrogenase while yolk sac tumors produce alpha fetoprotein.
steps.tx: Characteristic serum markers for dysgerminoma include **LDH**, **PLAP** (placental alkaline phosphatase), and beta-hCG (secreted by **syncytiotrophoblastic giant cells** in up to **5** percent of cases) alongside **normal AFP**, providing essential diagnostic distinction from yolk sac tumors, immature teratomas, and mixed embryonal carcinomas.

rows: Fibrous septa with mature lymphocytes; Fried-egg cells
Both AFP and beta-hCG markedly elevated
Sheets of pleomorphic primitive epithelial-like cells

steps.say: Yolk sac tumors represent biologically aggressive malignancies that secrete high levels of alpha fetoprotein. Histological examination reveals pathognomonic glomeruloid microstructures known as Schiller Duval bodies.
steps.tx: **Yolk sac tumor** (**endodermal sinus** tumor) represents the second most common MOGCT, universally characterized by rapid abdominal distension, **elevated serum AFP**, and pathognomonic **Schiller-Duval bodies** consisting of a glomerulus-like central capillary encircled by primitive columnar epithelial cells within an endodermal sinus space.

nodes.label: Present with rapid pelvic mass and acute lower abdominal pain
Document extreme elevation in serum alpha-fetoprotein (AFP >1000 ng/mL)
Identify Schiller-Duval bodies and PAS-positive hyaline globules on biopsy
Initiate urgent fertility-sparing surgery followed by mandatory platinum chemotherapy

steps.say: Given the young age of affected patients, preservation of reproductive potential is the paramount surgical objective. Unilateral salpingo-oophorectomy is standard even in advanced stage disease.
steps.tx: **Fertility-sparing surgery** comprising **unilateral salpingo-oophorectomy** with **contralateral ovarian preservation** and uterine conservation is standard across **all stages MOGCT** (Stage I through Stage IV), because extreme sensitivity to combination platinum chemotherapy preserves curative potential without requiring radical bilateral pelvic gonadectomy or hysterectomy.

left.title: Fertility-Sparing Staging (USO)
points: Unilateral salpingo-oophorectomy with preservation of uterus and opposite ovary
Comprehensive surgical staging: peritoneal cytology, omentectomy, nodal sampling
Safe in Stage I through Stage IV due to extreme chemosensitivity

right.title: Contraindicated Interventions
points: Routine wedge biopsy of normal-appearing contralateral ovary
Bilateral oophorectomy in young patients without proven bilateral involvement
Aggressive debulking causing extensive pelvic visceral damage

steps.say: Routine biopsy of the normal contralateral ovary must be avoided during surgical staging. Unnecessary wedge resection compromises ovarian follicular reserve.
steps.tx: There is a strict **contraindication to wedge biopsy** of a **normal contralateral ovary** in MOGCT staging, because wedge resection induces mechanical pelvic adhesions and causes iatrogenic infertility, compromising future **preservation of ovarian reserve** without yielding meaningful occult diagnostic findings in young women.

rows: Inspect and palpate only; DO NOT BIOPSY
Prevents tubal-ovarian adhesion and follicular loss
Preserves functional ovarian parenchyma if benign
Provides accurate surgical staging for adjuvant decision
Sample only grossly enlarged or suspicious nodes

steps.say: Patients with completely resected early stage pure dysgerminoma have an extraordinary prognosis without systemic treatment. Active surveillance avoids unnecessary chemotherapy exposure.
steps.tx: In **Stage IA dysgerminoma** (pure encapsulated tumor completely resected with negative staging), postoperative **observation alone** with **omission of adjuvant chemo** is standard, achieving a **cure rate >95%** (cure rate **1**00% with **95** percent salvage rate upon relapse using standard BEP chemotherapy).

left.title: Stage IA Pure Dysgerminoma (Active Surveillance)
points: Capsule intact, negative peritoneal cytology, negative lymph nodes
Avoids gonadotoxicity, pulmonary fibrosis, and secondary leukemia
Serial abdominal-pelvic CT and serum LDH monitoring

right.title: All Non-Dysgerminomas & Advanced Dysgerminoma
points: Yolk sac tumors, embryonal carcinomas, or Stage IB-IV dysgerminoma
Mandatory adjuvant BEP chemotherapy regardless of stage (except Stage I G1 teratoma)

steps.say: Unlike dysgerminoma, yolk sac tumors require mandatory systemic chemotherapy regardless of stage. The combination of bleomycin, etoposide, and cisplatin prevents lethal recurrence.
steps.tx: In **yolk sac tumor adjuvant chemo**, there is **mandatory adjuvant therapy** with the BEP regimen for all patients regardless of stage, because rapid **hematogenous dissemination** and intrinsic aggressive biology lead to fatal relapse in over ninety percent of patients managed with surgery alone.

nodes.label: Document histological confirmation of yolk sac tumor
Obtain baseline serum AFP and pulmonary function tests (DLCO)
Administer 3 cycles of BEP for completely resected stage I disease
Deliver 4 cycles of BEP for bulky or metastatic disease

steps.say: Adolescent females presenting with dysgerminoma require cytogenetic analysis to evaluate for underlying gonadal dysgenesis. The presence of a Y chromosome mandates bilateral gonadectomy.
steps.tx: Mandatory **karyotyping in dysgerminoma** is indicated in children and young adolescents with primary amenorrhea: discovering **Swyer syndrome 46,XY** (karyotype **46**,XY) or mixed gonadal dysgenesis carries a **30** percent risk of bilateral malignancy, mandating **bilateral gonadectomy** to eliminate lethal **gonadoblastoma** and dysgerminoma transformation.
